newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti says banks are being supportive.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti says banks are being supportive.

text.p: Indebted Italian high-tech group Olivetti said banks were taking an attitude of "positive support" even though the company was clearly "under close observation by the financial world."

Corporate finance director Luciano La Noce told a meeting of financial analysts he did not agree with talk that the company was "short of ready cash," adding that there were "no particular problems with Olivetti's suppliers."
He said the company has not yet had a meeting with all its creditor banks but "only bilateral meetings."
Olivetti announced late on Monday that its debt had surged to 2.39 trillion lire at the end of August from 1.26 trillion in June, and confirmed its first half 1996 pre-tax loss of 440.2 billion lire.
La Noce said that before publication of the interim results the banks "had a wait-and-see attitude... now each will make its own analysis."
Referring to the debts, he said Olivetti's financial sources had changed from those used in the past and that in the last two years "the financing mix has moved from bond issues towards the banks."
